slides.title: 5 holiday lights and tree myths to drop this year

slides.myth: LED holiday lights don't really save much power.
slides.fact: They use far less electricity than old incandescent strings. DOE figured 90% or more savings on a 6-foot tree over a 40-day season.
slides.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Energy Saver

slides.myth: You can plug as many light strings end to end as you want.
slides.fact: Every set has a limit. Read the maker's instructions for how many strands can be connected, and use lights with a testing lab label.

slides.myth: An artificial tree can't catch fire.
slides.fact: Many are fire resistant, but only if the label says so. Look for that statement when you buy one, and keep it away from heat.

slides.myth: A real tree that looked fresh at the lot will stay safe.
slides.fact: Check the stand's water every day. NIST fire tests show a well-watered tree is far less of a fire hazard than a dry one.

slides.myth: It's fine to leave the tree lights on all night.
slides.fact: Turn them off before you go to bed or leave the house. A timer makes it automatic and saves power too.
